root_cause: VCP's `inputMode: true` captures the Tab keydown event on the input and calls preventDefault(), blocking default focus traversal. The previous fix set `inputMode: false` which restored Tab navigation but broke click-to-show because VCP no longer handles click on the input element.
repair_strategy: Set `inputMode: false` to allow Tab key propagation, and add a click handler on the input element that explicitly calls `show()` to open the calendar, preserving pointer interaction while fixing keyboard navigation.
expected_accessibility_effect: Tab key moves focus from the date field to the next form field (#passengers) per WCAG 2.1.1, while clicking the date field still opens the calendar for pointer users.
functional_risks: Click handler might conflict if VCP still processes click (mitigated by inputMode=false)
Focus-in handler (EVENT_FOCUSIN_DATA_API) also shows calendar on focus; both triggers call show() which is idempotent
Inline datepickers unaffected (inputMode already false for inline)
verification_requirements: Tab key press on focused date field moves focus to next form field (#passengers)
Clicking the date field shows the calendar (date button visible)
Clicking a date in the calendar updates the input field value correctly
Initial date value (2026-10-22) is properly parsed and displayed on load
Inline datepickers (if present) remain functional for mouse interaction
